## Entry 5859 - assistant - 2026-09-03T15:59:45.568Z

*uuid=`b9f53661-e4f3-4842-b28d-d633bbd618cd` - branch=`HEAD` - model=`claude-opus-5`*

**text:**
```
That reframes the product, and I think it's the most important thing you've said today.

**It isn't a viewer. It's a scoping sandbox.** Load a real REPD line, then move it, then change its demand, and watch the grid answer change. That's early-stage scoping engineering with the feel of a sandbox — "not a game" is the right disclaimer, because the numbers are consequential.

Some of it may already exist. The estate has `grid-finding-scope-on-a-blank-click` in its capability list and a SCOPE control in the UI — so arbitrary-point compute may be built already, which would make "move the project" mostly a matter of binding an existing capability to a moved marker. And v9.89 just made the measurement technology-agnostic, so it should accept a bare coordinate without caring what's there. The agent's first job is to establish what exists versus what's genuinely new, because that division decides the size of the work.

**On capacity, I've told it to be blunt.** `capacity_mw` arrives in the deep link and is displayed — but it may be display-only. If changing it doesn't legitimately affect anything with the data the estate holds, the spec must say so. *A sandbox that pretends an input matters is worse than one that admits it doesn't yet.*

**And one constraint I made outrank every feature:** the moment a reader moves a project or edits its capacity, they're looking at something that doesn't exist. If a screenshot of a moved 840 MW scheme at a new location can pass for a consented one, the platform has manufactured a false planning claim — precisely the trust failure you've said would destroy it. So the spec must define how a scenario is marked, what happens to the REPD reference when it moves, and what a *shared link* of a modified scenario carries. A deep link that silently encodes a moved project is dangerous; one that says "scenario, not record" is a feature.

**This also makes your backend point decisive rather than merely correct.** Recompute-on-drag is impossible if every answer costs a 4 MiB download and a re-derivation on the handset. Interactive what-if forces the engine server-side. The two agents are now both scoped against that.

To the architecture agent I sent the presentation half: full-screen as the *default state* rather than a mode, and self-minimising chrome specified as real behaviour — trigger, animation budget, and an explicit rule that nothing mid-edit or carrying an unread result may auto-collapse. Auto-collapse is also what makes 1000 layers tolerable: a panel that opens on demand and closes itself is a different proposition from a permanent list.

Two things I told it never to design away, at any size, including the watch: a **recomputing** state that's honest rather than showing a stale number, and the **scenario-versus-record** marker.
```

```
Go is the right frame — you play shape and influence, and read deeply only where it's forced. I've been reading out variations across the whole board.
```

## Entry 5878 - assistant - 2026-09-03T16:00:49.788Z

*uuid=`368f4654-5b80-439a-a119-0cda98c85a0b` - branch=`HEAD` - model=`claude-opus-5`*

**text:**
```
Sent the same correction to the sandbox agent — go use the thing, let the spec fall out of what resists you.

The deeper point lands too: Go is bounded and this isn't. Exhaustive reading fails here *in principle*, not just in practice — so confidence built from specification is often false confidence, while surprise from playing is real information. Every correction I've had to make today came from someone touching the product, never from me reasoning harder.

Three agents are out playing rather than planning: one clicking through as a naive phone user with no access to the code, one prototyping skins in your Chrome, one about to go drag a project around and see what breaks.

I'll keep my hands off the board until they come back with shape.
```

## Entry 5886 - assistant - 2026-09-03T16:03:03.984Z

*uuid=`fd026142-5117-4c67-9992-3ad516f13dd6` - branch=`HEAD` - model=`claude-opus-5`*

**text:**
```
That frame names the failure mode precisely, better than "a skip is not a pass" did.

`technology_layer.enabled` reported `true` while the layer was off. It looked like a measurement and collapsed nothing. The state was never seen — so 32.7% of the spine stayed in superposition, green on every proof that read the field, broken for every reader who arrived.

And the day's real findings all have the shape you're describing — one local measurement, a counterpart far away, resolving on being seen:

- `document.hidden` set on this laptop revealed a failure on your phone that nobody could reach.
- One commit's stamp revealed 125 across the estate.
- One `.gitattributes` predicate revealed a whole class of wrong-question instruments.
- One field read honestly revealed 2,508 rows.

None required traversing the space. Each required the instrument actually touching the state.

So the working rule I'll hold: **measure the thing in front of me, honestly, and stop trying to enumerate what's beyond it.** The estate's 36 recorded failures were every one an instrument that reported without reading — which is the only way the far side stays hidden.

Three agents are out measuring. I'll wait for what they see rather than predict it.
```

```
Waiting for what they see.
```

## Entry 5979 - assistant - 2026-09-03T16:13:12.410Z

**text:**
```
Playing found more in thirteen minutes than my specifications did all afternoon.

**Move-the-project already works.** `__GRIDATLAS_NEON_LINKS__.selectAt(...)` is public on the page. It put Botley West in a field 40 km away and re-derived the entire card — nearest subs, nearest 400 kV, corridor estimate, ETYS join, site-wide envelope — in **3.7 ms across 5,800 substations**. Every honesty sentence travelled unprompted and **re-counted itself for the new place**. Nothing had to be taught to move.

**And a live danger.** The moved card read:

> *Botley West… 840 MW · OX29 4DZ · Oxfordshire · **REPD 12588 · application submitted** · FECKENHAM SUBSTATION…*

Real reference, real address, real planning status — sitting above a measurement to a substation **in another county**. The measurement block moved; the identity block didn't. The URL never changed, so a shared link reloads the true project while a screenshot carries the false one. Reachable from any console today. Console-only, so not casually exposed — but it's the exact artefact you said would destroy institutional trust, and it exists now.

**Grid At Point answers from a different dataset than the card.** NESO's 886 published connection points (502 located), not the OSM payload. At one coordinate: nearest OSM substation ≥33 kV **3.71 km**; nearest NESO connection point **30.5 km**. Both correct, different things counted, and neither card mentions the other. **Three arbitrary-point answers, two datasets, three routes** — the gap is composition, not compute.

**Capacity drives nothing**, checked four ways. Cards at 8 / 840 / 5,000 MW are byte-identical, and DC injection shares match to six decimals — necessarily, since `share = flow_mw / mw` over a linear solve. The one honest capacity number that exists, `flow_mw` against `published_ratings_mva` (458 MW on a 1,746 MVA circuit at 840 MW), is **already computed and already discarded**. That's yours to call.

**And a correction to what I told you.** I said interactive what-if forces the compute server-side. Wrong, and backwards: 0.5 / 3.7 / 13–20 / 8.8 ms all on-device, against 40–200 ms for a round trip. **Moving it server-side would make it worse.** Your backend point still holds — but for the 4.09 MiB cold start, which is a different track entirely.

**Two live defects found in passing:** a zero-feature map click returns at `:5847` *before* the scope branch at `:5864` — so the blank click that SCOPE and GRID AT POINT are named for lands in `clearLinks()` and **destroys the reader's card** (confirmed live, popups 1→0). And `armGridScope` never writes `grid_scope_armed`, so the page misreports its own mode.

The order changed after playing: arbitrary point moved from last to third, composed card to second, and **marking ships before drag and capacity — stated as non-negotiable**. Which is right: the machinery to move a project is already there, so the only thing standing between today and a falsifiable screenshot is the marking.

`sessions/202609031612-scenario-sandbox/00-SCOPE.md` (`02926c0`). One agent running, one wrapping up.
```

````
<result>Committed and pushed. Wrapping up here.

## What was built and verified

**`sessions/202609031559-skin-architecture/00-SKINS.md`** plus a working prototype, committed as `2fe3e37` (pushed). To open it:

```
cd C:/Users/vikra/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/claude/sessions/202609031559-skin-architecture/prototype
python -m http.server 8731 --bind 127.0.0.1
```
→ `http://127.0.0.1:8731/index.html` (a server is required, not `file://` — a skin is a separate `.json` fetched at runtime, which is the point). The server is currently running and the page is open in tab `1838138131`. Try `?skin=glanceable`, `?skin=tenfoot`.

## The headline finding — the seam stops one function short

v9.89 did the hard half: `link.measure.nearestSubstations(lon, lat, subs)` reads no technology at all, and that seam holds. But the four functions immediately downstream **return HTML strings** — `nearestScope()` (`sld-sandbox:2543`), `corridorBeside()` (`:2333`), `caveatHtml()` (`:3798`), `declaredBlockHtml()` (`:2562`). The measurement is data; **the sentences that make the measurement honest are markup**, welded to one class vocabulary and one length. A skin can place a `&lt;p class="neon-caveat"&gt;`; it cannot re-lay it out.

**If the estate does one thing from this document, it should be changing those four return shapes to data, with the current card as the first consumer and a value-for-value parity gate.** That is smaller than any skin and unblocks all of them.

## Detection matrix (measured, Chromium 152, this laptop)

Trustworthy: all pointer/hover queries, `maxTouchPoints`, `screen.*`, `dpr 1.5`, `prefers-*`, orientation. **Lies or useless:** `outerWidth/Height` returned `0×0`; `connection.downlink 10 / rtt 100` are clamp values, not measurements; `userAgentData.mobile:false` is shared by tablet, car, TV and fridge; `innerWidth` is **stale on a background tab** (two tabs reported 1707 and 2327 in a 563-px window).

**A TV and this laptop report identical `pointer: fine` + `hover: hover`.** So do a control-room wall and a laptop. Detection reliably identifies *a phone* and nothing else — which is the whole argument for the switcher.

## The gestureless-fullscreen defect — confirmed, and removed by construction

Confirmed in source at `sld-sandbox:6011–6014`: touch arrival calls `enterFullscreen()` with no gesture, the shell applies `fs-active`/`is-fullscreen` **before** `requestFullscreen()` rejects into an empty `.catch(()=&gt;{})`, and nothing removes them. My prototype has **no call site for the Fullscreen API at all** — full-bleed is the default CSS layout of every skin. Not verified on a real touch device; verified as mechanism.

## The Winamp test

Skins 2 and 3 each cost **one JSON file plus one filename in a manifest array**. `engine.js` contains no skin id. Parity with live: **Cowley Substation 15.757 km** vs live 15.76; corridor 19.62 vs live 19.6; coverage 502/886 = 56.7%.

The strongest idea: **the honesty contract is enforced at the seam by the engine.** `FIELDS['measurement.headline'].mandatory_with = ['qualifier.straight','qualifier.sample','qualifier.scenario']`, checked before render. `skins/broken-compact.json` — a plausible compact skin that drops the sentences — is **refused with all three reasons**. And the glanceable skin carries all three qualifiers **unclipped at 320×320**: a watch does not have to drop anything.

## 1000 layers

Registry built and proved at 1000 synthetic entries. Declared = **136.7 KiB** of manifest; the same thousand with payloads = **1.18 GiB**. **18 DOM rows existed while 1000 were declared.** Minimise retains the payload (presentation); unload releases it (engine act, always reported). Paint budget 24 / memory 120; the paint ceiling **refuses by naming what to turn off** rather than dropping silently. Health is read back from the map adapter — there is a button that corrupts a layer behind the registry's back to reproduce the `technology_layer.enabled === true while off` false green, and `health()` catches it.

## Not verified — stated plainly

`document.hidden` was **true all session**; four Win32 foregrounding routes failed, so **no live-Atlas geometry is quoted**. No touch device, so every `pointer:coarse` claim is unverified for a fifth session. MapLibre per-layer cost unmeasured, so the budgets are reasoned starting values. Deep-link null-island and `zoom` guards not ported. No desktop no-regression run. The ten-foot skin **overflows** at 640×360 (558/212) — recorded unfixed, because fixing it is two numbers in a JSON file and that is itself the proof.

Two method notes are written into §1.2–1.3 so they outlive this task: the iframe narrow-viewport method (re-verified at 320 px), and a correction — the estate's foregrounding recipe did not work today, and a `DllImport` of `GetWindowTextW` without `CharSet=CharSet.Unicode` returns **only the first character of every window title**, which made my first sweep report zero Chrome windows.

Screenshots: `C:\Users\vikra\AppData\Local\Temp\claude-chrome-screenshots-rkhfxg\screenshot-1788451708314-15.jpg` (switcher and auto-chosen badge), `...-17.jpg` (stage; the tab's browser zoom was changed by another lane mid-session so it is cropped — the substance was verified programmatically, not from the image).</result>
````

## Entry 6061 - user - 2026-09-03T17:11:00.484Z

*uuid=`bf6cffea-01a4-403b-b03f-b8510262b225` - branch=`HEAD`*

**text:**
```
<task-notification>
<task-id>abc648e6299765235</task-id>
<tool-use-id>toolu_01LVBDwN3QHpkfnkWZM8GUNx</tool-use-id>
<output-file>C:\Users\vikra\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-vikra\5b94bee7-197b-4cfd-944b-d4cf3aa02d18\tasks\abc648e6299765235.output</output-file>
<status>completed</status>
<summary>Agent "Naive mobile user pain-point testing" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>Done. Committed as `e922de8` at `sessions/202609031710-user-pain-log/00-PAIN.md` (with 13 screenshots alongside). The pre-existing untracked/modified files were left alone.

**Emulation was genuine, and verified in-page before anything was tested:** 393×852 @3x, `pointer: coarse` **true**, `hover: none`, `maxTouchPoints` 5, iPhone Safari UA, `document.hidden` false at every measurement. No finding needs the "narrow viewport" caveat. I had to launch a separate Chrome with a CDP port — the user's own Chrome exposes none, and the extension gives no emulation control.

**101 MAP taps across all 25 technologies** (5 spine tabs + all 20 in the wider-fleet dropdown), 5 random rows each, or every row where fewer than 5 exist. 99 reached a map; 2 landed on greyed `NO MAP` rows.

The headline findings:

1. **The answer never lands on screen. 99/99.** The grid distance was present somewhere on the page every single time and visible without scrolling zero times. It sits ~900 px down in a card whose bottom edge is ~390 px below the phone. **Swiping up on the card does not move it** — scrollTop stayed at exactly 0 through every attempt (I proved swipes work on this product first: 935 px per flick on the list). The only route I found was dragging the card by its title bar, a desktop gesture.
2. **Four floating bars print over the card's text on every load** — the TOOLS/GRID/SUBS/SCOPE/CLEAR row, GB PRICES, VERSIONS, HIDE LAYERS, plus the credit line stamped across the words.
3. **Performing that drag buries the close button** under the search box — tapping × opens the keyboard instead.
4. **The record counter lies after any wider-fleet choice**: 4 of 4 tried left it quoting the previous technology (`3,563 of 7,680 records · largest 840 MW` above a table of 1 flywheel project). Spine tabs update it correctly, so it is specific to the dropdown.
5. **Offshore projects open onto a featureless grey screen** — Berwick Bank at 28 s had no coast, no labels, nothing.
6. MAP is column 13 of 13 in a 1,680 px table inside a 347 px window: **four sideways flicks, and the project name is gone when you arrive**.

Also: 56/100 rows show inert `GRID –`/`SUB –` whose only explanation is a hover tooltip a phone can never trigger; 31/927 rows have no MAP (15/100 on OFFSHORE, 14/100 on ALL TECH, 0 on 22 technologies); 137 of 149 map controls are under 44 px including 126 checkboxes at 17×17; 99/99 loads had layers stuck on `[WAIT]`; and the wider-fleet rows carry no GRID/SUB readout at all.

Two caveats stated in the report: fine-grained timing covers roughly half the loads (the machine ran out of memory mid-run and I made each observation cheaper), and because Chrome pauses tabs opened via `target=_blank` in a way that blocked emulation, I confirmed the tap opens a tab with a real touch event and then observed the identical URL in a verified-iPhone tab.</result>
<usage><subagent_tokens>325241</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>274</tool_uses><duration_ms>4484137</duration_ms></usage>
</task-notification>
```

```
Yes. Now I have.

`3.43 km`, in a `span.neon-km`, sitting at **y = 1502 in an 852px viewport** — 650px below the bottom of the screen. `html` and `body` are both `overflow: hidden`, and `window.scrollTo(0, 9999)` left `scrollTop` at `0`. The page cannot scroll.

**But my own eyes caught something the pain agent couldn't**, because it was forbidden from diagnosing: `div.maplibregl-popup-content` **is** scrollable — `overflow-y: auto`, scrollHeight 1811 against clientHeight 808 — and when I drove it programmatically it moved, **0 → 1002.67**.

So the content isn't unscrollable. **The gesture never reaches it.** That popup sits on the MapLibre canvas, and the map takes the drag for panning before the popup sees it. That reframes the fix.
```

## Entry 6198 - assistant - 2026-09-03T17:43:55.721Z

*uuid=`bb006e3b-35f3-4546-a1a3-9cb72f390f54` - branch=`HEAD` - model=`claude-opus-5`*

**text:**
```
What my own eyes added, beyond confirming it:

**The pain agent reported "the card does not scroll."** True from a user's side — `scrollTop` stayed at 0 through every swipe. But it was forbidden from diagnosing, so that's where it stopped.

**The card has 1,003px of scroll range sitting unused.** `maplibregl-popup-content` is `overflow-y: auto` with scrollHeight 1811 against clientHeight 808. Driven from script it moves fine. So this isn't a layout defect — it's almost certainly **MapLibre consuming the touch gesture for map panning before the popup's scroller ever sees it.**

That makes the fix small: stop propagation of `touchstart`/`touchmove` on the popup content, or set `touch-action` on it. Not a card restructure, and it touches none of the honesty sentences.

**What I proved and what I didn't:** proved the 650px offset, the `overflow: hidden` on html and body, and the unused scroll range. **Not** proved that MapLibre eats the gesture — my iframe gives a real 393px viewport but `pointer: coarse` is false, so I generated no touch events. I've told the fixer to confirm capture before fixing it, and to reconcile against the pain log's real-touch run.

And the deeper thing stands regardless: even scrolled, a reader travels 1,502px past envelope detail and a duplicated title to reach the number the product exists to state. Fixing the gesture makes the answer *reachable*. It doesn't make it *land*.

You were right to ask. I'd been relaying for three hours, and the one thing I'd personally verified before this — "only three technologies" — was wrong.
```

## Entry 6272 - assistant - 2026-09-03T17:52:39.204Z

*uuid=`4acacb52-9185-4c08-9815-49d901220739` - branch=`HEAD` - model=`claude-opus-5`*

**text:**
```
Refuted **structurally**, which is stronger than the empirical refutation — three independent exclusions:

**Topology** — `canvasContainer.contains(popupContent)` is `false`. The popup is a *sibling* of the canvas container; the card's bubble path never traverses it.

**Registration** — maplibre-gl 3.6.2 binds its touch listeners to `getCanvasContainer()`. The only `document`/`window` entries in the bundle are mouse and blur. **No document-level touch listener exists**, so capture-phase interception above the popup is impossible.

**CSS** — `touch-action` computes to `auto` at every level from the popup content up to `html`. MapLibre's `touch-action: none` lands on the sibling again. And zero touch handlers across all shell scripts and four cartridges.

**Consuming element: none.** All three fixes I proposed are dead. Your overlap is the whole defect.

Two things worth keeping:

**A new measurement** — at 393px the card's rect is `left −87, width 330`. It hangs **87px off the left edge** as well as being overlapped at the bottom. Both are fixed by the docked full-width sheet now shipping, but that's a second reason it's the right fix.

**A methodological catch that doesn't bite, but nearly did.** This agent noted that JS-constructed `TouchEvent`s are *untrusted and can never move `scrollTop` natively* — so "dispatch touch, watch scrollTop" is not a valid discriminator, and it refused to use it as one. The implementer's flick table used CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, which goes through the browser's real input pipeline and *is* trusted. So both stand, by different routes, and agree. Had the implementer used the JS route, its table would have been a confident artefact.

Cleanup verified — no debug Chrome, harness removed, its tab closed, and it correctly identified a neighbouring tab as another agent's and left it alone.

Committed `c04c360`. One agent shipping, one closing out.
```

```
**Worse than the console route in two ways.** The URL carries the state, so a share propagates the falsehood rather than healing it. And the camera flies to the *register's* coordinates while the pin — labelled with the real project name — and all five neon links are drawn at `[−1.6, 52.1]`, 36 km outside the visible bounds. The reader sees an Oxfordshire map, an Oxfordshire address and a Worcestershire measurement, with nothing on screen contradicting any of it.
```

## Entry 6328 - assistant - 2026-09-03T18:05:17.045Z

*uuid=`6b38a3be-fabb-42e7-8f37-2a8be29a344f` - branch=`HEAD` - model=`claude-opus-5`*

**text:**
```
**v9.90 is live and green, verified independently.** Generation `202609031751`, all three workflows `success` on `d5f2d1d`.

And I nearly filed a false alarm on the size guard. `wc -c` gave 369,907 against a 368,640 ceiling — 1,267 **over**. But that counts bytes, and this cartridge is full of multi-byte glyphs. In characters, which is what a JS length check measures: **366,434 — exactly the agent's figure, and under.** Same in the blob, zero CR either side. My instrument was wrong, not the number.

That's the fourth time today a wrong predicate nearly became a finding, and the second time it was mine.

**What actually landed, measured on a verified device at `pointer:coarse`:**

| | v9.89 | v9.90 |
|---|---|---|
| measurement | y 906–1014, **off screen** | **y 555–650, in view, topmost** |
| scope sentence | off screen | **y 659–713, in view** |
| `.map-controls` over card | **42,047 px²** | **0** |
| left clip at 390px | −89px | none |
| thumb-zone flick | **0** | **395–422px at all six points** |

Desktop unchanged in geometry, with the answer moving y=780 → y=521. And it discarded its own first live run because `document.hidden` came back `true`, added `Page.bringToFront`, and re-measured — the discipline that has cost this session more than any product bug.

**On P2 it found something that changes the fix, and it's asking before writing.** `filtered` holds **indices into the spine's own payload**. Wider-fleet rows come from a different payload and aren't in that index space at all — so "have the cartridge write into `filtered`" isn't available. And the cartridge's own text already says county, town, postcode and REPD ref "are withheld rather than guessed" for these rows, so they *cannot* fill the spine's 50-column schema.

Its proposal: one spine entry point taking `{count, capacity, largest, exportProvider}` — which fixes the counter, the state, the contradiction **and the gauge arcs for free** — with the wider fleet supplying a provider that **declines, naming the columns it can't carry.**

I'm approving that, including the refusal. Refusing beats 3,563 solar rows under a flywheel heading, and it beats a half-empty CSV that leaves the platform looking authoritative. It matches the precedent already in that cartridge. **But it does remove a button's function on a public page** — so if you'd rather it degraded differently, say now and I'll hold it.
```

```
**Confirmed in the live served bytes.** `origin_source` present three times, `origin_discrepancy_km` once, and the old conditional guard — `isFiniteNumber(linkLon)` — is **gone: zero references**. The fix is deployed, not just committed.

**Correcting myself twice:** I told you nothing was pushed and that gridatlas held uncommitted work one `git checkout` from being lost. Both wrong — that agent finished and shipped before the halt reached it. The tree is clean at `65786ae`, matching origin.

**What v9.91 actually does, measured against the deployed release:**

| the attack URL | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| measurement | **Feckenham · 30.50 km** | **Cowley · 15.76 km** |
| `nearest_km` | 3.708 | **3.432** — the true value |
| `origin_source` | undefined | **`register`** |
| `origin_discrepancy_km` | undefined | **36.274** |

The identity and the measurement are now the same place by construction. All four arrival shapes checked for regressions — the true link unchanged, `repd_ref`-only unchanged, coordinates-only carries no address or planning status so no false claim is possible. The v9.90 phone sheet survives intact.

It also caught that one of its own checks was asserting the defect: *"the identity fallback is gated on `repd_ref` being present"* was testing the very guard that caused this. It now asserts the register is consulted for **every** link, and that the old form is absent from the served bytes.

**The ceiling decision is now concrete, and it's yours:**

- `sld-sandbox`: **368,149 / 368,640 — 491 characters left.**
- `substation-intelligence`: 233,269 / 400,000 — **166,731 spare.**
- `sld-sandbox` carries **18,148 characters of stylesheet** in template literals, 8,456 in a single `installStyles` block. That's presentation sitting in the file that's out of room.

Moving those into a module carried by `substation-intelligence` is the same move v9.85 made with the version ledger, and returns ~10,000 characters of headroom. It deliberately didn't do it — *"I'd rather not bundle an architectural hoist into a security fix."* Correct instinct.

**Still open:** the console route (`selectAt` still moves the measurement under an unmoved identity block), and the CSV export. `pipelinenews` has zero tracked changes.

Everything is stopped now. Live: **gridatlas v9.91** and **pipelinenews `202609031308`**, both green.
```

```
Commissioned. Three deliverables, and the third is the one that actually answers "wtf happened":

**1. The full thread rendered** — every message, tool call and result verbatim, thinking blocks marked. The earlier render stopped at 09:40Z with 5,051 entries; the session has grown enormously since, so it supersedes or extends that, and must say which rather than leave two files disagreeing about coverage.

**2. The Parquet refreshed** and `verify_memory_store.py` run to exit 0, so it stays queryable across all sessions rather than being a wall of text.

**3. `SESSION-INDEX.md`** — because a fresh session won't read 30,000 rows. A chronological index with evidence pointers: what shipped and is live (with URLs and runner conclusions), what's still open, one line per session directory, the uncommitted state left in each working tree — and the method traps, because those cost this session more than any product bug did:

- `resize_window` reports success and changes nothing — five sessions lost to that
```
